Innovation
Air tools, which have been the workhorses of most manufacturing and construction shops, are now becoming an important part of the process toolbox for both do-it-yourselfers and professionals. In some cases, they have replaced large, expensive, highly power-hungry stationary machinery as the tool of choice.
They are now being used for welding, grinding, sanding, cutting, contouring, deburring, finishing, removing burrs and even for welding and heat treatment. That's a huge range of tasks, many of which have previously been performed using a stand-alone machine or by hand. Airtools also allow craftsmen to work in confined spaces, work without a power supply nearby or even to work in tight areas where a stand-alone piece of equipment just won't fit.
